chunks: And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him) [exhorting people to jihad to return to Siffin]: It has been related by Nawf al-Bikālī that he said:

Amīr al-mu’minīn ‘Alī (peace be upon him) delivered this sermon to us at Kūfah while standing on a stone that Ja‘dah ibn Hubayrah al-Makhzūmī had placed for him. He had a woollen apparel on his body, the belt of his sword was made of leaves, and the sandals on his feet too were of palm leaves. His forehead had a hardened spot like that of a camel (on its knee, due to too many and long prostrations). He said (peace be upon him):

key_terms.ثَفِنَةُ بَعِيرٍ: The callus/hardened spot on a camel's knee/forehead
key_terms.جَعْدَةُ بْنُ هُبَيْرَةَ: Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah (a companion who placed the stone)
key_terms.حَمَائِلُ السَّيْفِ: The belt or strap of the sword
key_terms.مِدْرَعَةٌ: A type of woollen garment or coat of mail

ai.seo_question: What were the physical conditions and attire of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) when delivering his sermon in Kūfah?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha captures Imam Ali’s ascetic leadership during the pivotal period leading to the Battle of Siffin, where he stood on a simple stone erected stone to address the Kufans. The vivid description of his woolen coat, fiber sandals, and callused forehead serves as a tangible reminder of his spiritual authority and readiness for sacrifice, contrasting his humility with the political complexities of the era. This physical portrayal underscores the Shia emphasis on the Imam’s closeness to God and his people, framing the upcoming jihad not merely as a military campaign but as a spiritual struggle for justice.
